subproblem.title: Ball mass between blow-up integrals of cut-offs
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ a Borel measure on E that is finite on compact sets, x ∈ E, f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) and t > 0. (i) If f(z) ≤ 1 for all z and f(z) ≤ 0 whenever |z| > 1, then ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) ≤ μ(B_t(x)). (ii) If f(z) ≥ 0 for all z and f(z) ≥ 1 whenever |z| ≤ 1, then μ(B_t(x)) ≤ ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y). Here B_t(x) is the closed ball, μ(B_t(x)) is taken as a real number (μ.real), and the integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (x : Ambient n ℓ) (f : C_c(Ambient n ℓ, ℝ)) (t : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → 0 < t → ((∀ y : Ambient n ℓ, f y ≤ 1) → (∀ y : Ambient n ℓ, 1 < ‖y‖ → f y ≤ 0) → ∫ y, f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂μ ≤ μ.real (closedBall x t)) ∧ ((∀ y : Ambient n ℓ, 0 ≤ f y) → (∀ y : Ambient n ℓ, ‖y‖ ≤ 1 → 1 ≤ f y) → μ.real (closedBall x t) ≤ ∫ y, f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂μ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 3 (the sandwich (3.1)). Here it is stated for an arbitrary f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ), with the two cut-off inequalities as hypotheses; the parent applies it to its cut-offs f_δ⁻ and f_δ⁺. No errata apply.

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + ℓ)); B_t(x) := closedBall x t (closed ball); 1_A is the indicator of A, with value 1 on A and 0 elsewhere; μ.real(A) := (μ A).toReal; η(y) := t⁻¹(y − x); ∫ is the Bochner integral.
Hypotheses: μ is a measure on the Borel σ-algebra of E with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ); x ∈ E; f ∈ C_c(E, ℝ); t > 0.
Claim: (i) if f(z) ≤ 1 for all z and f(z) ≤ 0 whenever ‖z‖ > 1, then ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) ≤ μ.real(B_t(x)); (ii) if f(z) ≥ 0 for all z and f(z) ≥ 1 whenever ‖z‖ ≤ 1, then μ.real(B_t(x)) ≤ ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y).

Results used (pinned Mathlib; available under the frozen imports):
- Homeomorph.subRight, Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero, HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph.
- Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport: a continuous compactly supported function is integrable for a measure finite on compacts.
- IsCompact.measure_lt_top, MeasureTheory.integrable_indicator_iff, MeasureTheory.integrableOn_const.
- MeasureTheory.integral_indicator_one: ∫ 1_A dμ = μ.real(A) for measurable A.
- MeasureTheory.integral_mono.

Proof.
1. Integrability of the blow-up. η is a homeomorphism of E: the translation y ↦ y − x followed by the dilation z ↦ t⁻¹z, where t⁻¹ ≠ 0 (Homeomorph.subRight, Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero). Hence F := f∘η, that is F(y) = f(t⁻¹(y − x)), is continuous. It has compact support, because tsupport(f∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport f) is the image of the compact set tsupport f under the continuous map η⁻¹ (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). Since μ is finite on compact sets, F is μ-integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
2. The ball. B_t(x) is compact, so μ(B_t(x)) < ∞ (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). It is closed, hence measurable. Therefore 1_{B_t(x)} is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const), and ∫ 1_{B_t(x)} dμ = μ.real(B_t(x)) (integral_indicator_one).
3. Key equivalence. For y ∈ E, ‖η(y)‖ = t⁻¹‖y − x‖ because t⁻¹ > 0. So ‖η(y)‖ ≤ 1 ⟺ ‖y − x‖ ≤ t ⟺ y ∈ B_t(x).
4. Part (i). Assume f(z) ≤ 1 for all z and f(z) ≤ 0 whenever ‖z‖ > 1. Then F ≤ 1_{B_t(x)} pointwise. If y ∈ B_t(x), then F(y) = f(η(y)) ≤ 1 = 1_{B_t(x)}(y). If y ∉ B_t(x), then ‖η(y)‖ > 1 by step 3, so F(y) ≤ 0 = 1_{B_t(x)}(y). Both functions are integrable (steps 1 and 2), so integral_mono gives ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y) = ∫ F dμ ≤ ∫ 1_{B_t(x)} dμ = μ.real(B_t(x)).
5. Part (ii). Assume f(z) ≥ 0 for all z and f(z) ≥ 1 whenever ‖z‖ ≤ 1. Then 1_{B_t(x)} ≤ F pointwise. If y ∈ B_t(x), then ‖η(y)‖ ≤ 1 by step 3, so F(y) ≥ 1 = 1_{B_t(x)}(y). If y ∉ B_t(x), then 1_{B_t(x)}(y) = 0 ≤ F(y). By integral_mono, μ.real(B_t(x)) = ∫ 1_{B_t(x)} dμ ≤ ∫ F dμ = ∫ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) dμ(y).
6. Steps 4 and 5 are the two conjuncts of the claim. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the argument): every name above is available under the frozen imports. A suitable homeomorphism is η := (Homeomorph.subRight x).trans (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero t⁻¹ (inv_ne_zero ht.ne')); then the function y ↦ f (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) is f ∘ η.
proof_key_steps: y ↦ f(t⁻¹(y − x)) is f composed with a homeomorphism of E, so it is continuous with compact support and μ-integrable
B_t(x) is compact, so 1_{B_t(x)} is μ-integrable with ∫ 1_{B_t(x)} dμ = μ.real(B_t(x))
Under the hypotheses of (i), f(t⁻¹(y − x)) ≤ 1_{B_t(x)}(y) pointwise; under those of (ii), the reverse inequality holds; integrate both with integral_mono

audit.reason: The standalone one-line proposition exactly expresses both conditional inequalities, including compact support, finiteness on compacts, t > 0, and μ.real. The proof establishes integrability of the composition using the blow-up homeomorphism and integrability of the closed-ball indicator using compactness. Positive t gives the stated norm-membership equivalence; the two pointwise comparisons then yield both conclusions by integral monotonicity. No additional sign hypothesis on the lower cutoff is needed, and the proof is independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Hⁿ-measure of balls in an n-plane: Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0 be integers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, P a linear subspace of E with dim P = n (finrank P = n), and s ≥ 0. Then (Hⁿ⌞P)(B_s(0)) = Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ. Precisely, ((μHE[n]).restrict P)(closedBall 0 s) = ENNReal.ofReal(omega n · sⁿ), where Hⁿ = μHE[n], B_s(0) is the closed ball and ω_n = omega n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (s : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n → 0 ≤ s → ((μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)).restrict (P : Set (Ambient n ℓ))) (closedBall (0 : Ambient n ℓ) s) = ENNReal.ofReal (omega n * s ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof, step 1 (Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ; in the proof of the DAG node root.tangent_structure-a1 this fact is part of (R2)). No errata apply. Adaptation: the parent identifies the constant through the explicit Gamma-function formulas InnerProductSpace.volume_closedBall / InnerProductSpace.volume_ball. Those need the extra import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Lebesgue.VolumeOfBalls, which the parent's implementation note permits. The argument below reaches the same identity through a linear isometry P ≅ ℝⁿ and the scaling law of Haar measure, so it stays inside the frozen imports. It does not use n ≥ 1.

Conventions. n, ℓ ≥ 0 are integers; E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + ℓ)); ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; for a metric space X, Hⁿ_X := μHE[n] on X (used for X = E, for the subtype P, and for X = ℝⁿ); B_s(z) := closedBall z s (closed ball); ω_n := omega n = (Lⁿ(ball 0 1)).toReal; ν := (Hⁿ_E).restrict P = Hⁿ⌞P.
Hypotheses: P is a linear subspace of E with finrank P = n, and s ≥ 0.
Claim: ν(B_s(0)) = ENNReal.ofReal(ω_n · sⁿ), i.e. ((μHE[n]).restrict P)(closedBall 0 s) = ENNReal.ofReal(omega n * s ^ n).

Results used (pinned Mathlib; all available under the frozen imports; standard axioms only):
- Submodule.subtypeₗᵢ: the inclusion P → E as a linear isometry.
- Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure: for an isometry f : X → Y, (μHE[d]).map f = (μHE[d]).restrict (range f).
- MeasureTheory.Measure.map_apply.
- stdOrthonormalBasis, OrthonormalBasis.reindex, OrthonormalBasis.repr.
- LinearIsometryEquiv.image_closedBall.
- Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image: μHE[d](f '' A) = μHE[d](A) for an isometry f.
- EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume: μHE[d] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d).
- MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_closedBall: for an additive Haar measure λ on a finite-dimensional real normed space F and r ≥ 0, λ(closedBall x r) = ofReal(r^(finrank F)) · λ(ball 0 1).
- finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, MeasureTheory.measure_ball_lt_top, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, ENNReal.ofReal_mul.

Proof.
1. Reduction to the subspace. Let ι : P → E be the inclusion. It is a linear isometry (Submodule.subtypeₗᵢ), hence an isometry and continuous, and range ι = P as a subset of E. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, ν = (Hⁿ_E).restrict (range ι) = ι_*(Hⁿ_P). The closed ball B_s(0) is closed, hence Borel, and ι is measurable, so ν(B_s(0)) = Hⁿ_P(ι⁻¹(B_s(0))) (Measure.map_apply). Since ‖ι(p)‖ = ‖p‖ for p ∈ P, ι⁻¹(B_s(0)) = {p ∈ P : ‖p‖ ≤ s} = closedBall (0 : P) s. Hence ν(B_s(0)) = Hⁿ_P(closedBall (0 : P) s).
2. Transfer to ℝⁿ. The standard orthonormal basis of P is indexed by Fin (finrank P). Reindex it along the bijection Fin (finrank P) ≃ Fin n given by finrank P = n. This gives an orthonormal basis of P indexed by Fin n, whose coordinate map e := repr : P → ℝⁿ is a linear isometry equivalence. A linear isometry equivalence maps closedBall 0 s onto closedBall (e 0) s = closedBall 0 s (LinearIsometryEquiv.image_closedBall and e(0) = 0). Euclidean Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). Therefore Hⁿ_P(closedBall (0 : P) s) = Hⁿ_{ℝⁿ}(e(closedBall (0 : P) s)) = Hⁿ_{ℝⁿ}(closedBall (0 : ℝⁿ) s).
3. Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ. By EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Hⁿ_{ℝⁿ} = Lⁿ. Lⁿ is an additive Haar measure on ℝⁿ, and finrank ℝⁿ = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Since s ≥ 0, Measure.addHaar_closedBall gives Lⁿ(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(sⁿ) · Lⁿ(ball 0 1).
4. The constant. ball 0 1 is bounded, ℝⁿ is proper, and Lⁿ is finite on compact sets, so Lⁿ(ball 0 1) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). Hence Lⁿ(ball 0 1) = ofReal((Lⁿ(ball 0 1)).toReal) = ofReal(ω_n), by ENNReal.ofReal_toReal and the definition of omega n.
5. Conclusion. By steps 1–4, ν(B_s(0)) = ofReal(sⁿ) · ofReal(ω_n). Since sⁿ ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(sⁿ) · ofReal(ω_n) = ofReal(sⁿ · ω_n) = ofReal(ω_n · sⁿ). This is the claim ((μHE[n]).restrict P)(closedBall 0 s) = ENNReal.ofReal(omega n * s ^ n). Every cited result holds in every dimension, so the hypothesis n ≥ 1 is not needed. ∎

Implementation note (not part of the argument): every name above is available under the frozen imports, so no import needs to be added. A suitable isometry is e := ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ P).reindex (finCongr hP)).repr, where hP : finrank ℝ P = n.
proof_key_steps: The inclusion ι: P → E is an isometry with range P, so Hⁿ⌞P = ι_*(Hⁿ_P), and ι⁻¹(B_s(0)) = closedBall (0 : P) s
The reindexed standard orthonormal basis gives a linear isometry e: P ≅ ℝⁿ; it maps closedBall 0 s onto closedBall 0 s and preserves Hⁿ
On ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ, and Haar scaling gives Lⁿ(closedBall 0 s) = ofReal(sⁿ)·Lⁿ(ball 0 1)
Lⁿ(ball 0 1) is finite, so it equals ofReal(ω_n); hence the value is ofReal(sⁿ)·ofReal(ω_n) = ofReal(ω_n sⁿ)

subproblem.title: C_c cut-offs approximating Hⁿ(P ∩ B_1(0)) = ω_n from inside and outside
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ≥ 0, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, P a linear subspace of E with dim P = n, Hⁿ = μHE[n] and ω_n = omega n. (i) For every real a < ω_n there is g ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) with g(y) ≤ 1 for all y, g(y) ≤ 0 whenever |y| > 1, and a < ∫_P g dHⁿ. (ii) For every real b > ω_n there is h ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) with h(y) ≥ 0 for all y, h(y) ≥ 1 whenever |y| ≤ 1, and ∫_P h dHⁿ < b. Here ∫_P is the Bochner integral with respect to Hⁿ⌞P.

Source: the parent proof, steps 1, 2 and 4, together with the choice of δ in step 5. This is Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2): cut-offs f with f ≡ 1 on B_1(0) and f ≡ 0 off B_{1+ε}(0). No errata apply. The hypothesis n ≥ 1 is not used.

Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n + ℓ)); Hⁿ := μHE[n]; ν := Hⁿ⌞P = (μHE[n]).restrict P, so ∫_P u dHⁿ = ∫ u dν (Bochner integral); B_s(0) := closedBall 0 s; ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm of E; ω_n := omega n = (Lⁿ(ball 0 1)).toReal ≥ 0, where Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); ν.real(A) := (ν A).toReal; 1_A is the indicator of A, with value 1 on A.
Hypothesis: P is a linear subspace of E with finrank P = n.
Claim: (i) for every real a < ω_n there is g ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) with g(y) ≤ 1 for all y, g(y) ≤ 0 whenever ‖y‖ > 1, and a < ∫_P g dHⁿ; (ii) for every real b > ω_n there is h ∈ C_c(E, ℝ) with h(y) ≥ 0 for all y, h(y) ≥ 1 whenever ‖y‖ ≤ 1, and ∫_P h dHⁿ < b.

Results used:
- The sibling theorem Submission.ts_plane_closedBall_measure, of Lean type ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Ambient n ℓ)) (s : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n → 0 ≤ s → ((μHE[n] : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)).restrict (P : Set (Ambient n ℓ))) (closedBall (0 : Ambient n ℓ) s) = ENNReal.ofReal (omega n * s ^ n). That is: if finrank P = n and s ≥ 0, then ν(B_s(0)) = ENNReal.ofReal(ω_n sⁿ).
- Pinned Mathlib, available under the frozen imports: IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall, HasCompactSupport.intro.
- CompactlySupportedContinuousMap.integrable: elements of C_c are integrable for measures finite on compacts.
- MeasureTheory.integrable_indicator_iff, MeasureTheory.integrableOn_const, MeasureTheory.integral_indicator_one, MeasureTheory.integral_mono.

Proof.
1. Ball values. By the sibling theorem Submission.ts_plane_closedBall_measure, ν(B_s(0)) = ofReal(ω_n sⁿ) for every s ≥ 0. Since ω_n ≥ 0 (it is a toReal) and sⁿ ≥ 0, ν.real(B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ.
2. ν is finite on compact sets. A compact K ⊆ E is bounded, so K ⊆ B_R(0) for some R; replacing R by max(R, 0) we may assume R ≥ 0. Then ν(K) ≤ ν(B_R(0)) = ofReal(ω_n Rⁿ) < ∞. Consequently every element of C_c(E, ℝ) is ν-integrable. Moreover, for each s ≥ 0 the set B_s(0) is closed with ν(B_s(0)) < ∞, so 1_{B_s(0)} is ν-integrable and ∫ 1_{B_s(0)} dν = ν.real(B_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ.
3. Part (i). Let a < ω_n. The function δ ↦ ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ is continuous on ℝ and takes the value ω_n > a at δ = 0. So a < ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ for all δ in some neighbourhood of 0. Every neighbourhood of 0 meets (0, 1), so fix δ ∈ (0, 1) with a < ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ. Define g(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 − ‖y‖)/δ)) for y ∈ E.
 (a) g is continuous, as a composition of continuous functions.
 (b) If ‖y‖ > 1, then (1 − ‖y‖)/δ < 0, so max(0, (1 − ‖y‖)/δ) = 0 and g(y) = min(1, 0) = 0. Thus g vanishes outside the compact set B_1(0), so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro) and g ∈ C_c(E, ℝ). In particular g(y) ≤ 0 whenever ‖y‖ > 1.
 (c) g(y) ≤ 1 for all y, because g is a minimum with 1.
 (d) 1_{B_{1−δ}(0)} ≤ g pointwise. If ‖y‖ ≤ 1 − δ, then (1 − ‖y‖)/δ ≥ δ/δ = 1, so g(y) = 1. Otherwise 1_{B_{1−δ}(0)}(y) = 0 ≤ g(y), because min(1, max(0, ·)) ≥ 0.
 By (d), step 2 with s = 1 − δ > 0, and integral_mono: ∫_P g dHⁿ = ∫ g dν ≥ ∫ 1_{B_{1−δ}(0)} dν = ω_n(1 − δ)ⁿ > a. With (b) and (c), g has all the properties required in (i).
4. Part (ii). Let b > ω_n. The function δ ↦ ω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ is continuous and takes the value ω_n < b at δ = 0. As in step 3, fix δ ∈ (0, 1) with ω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ < b. Define h(y) := min(1, max(0, (1 + δ − ‖y‖)/δ)) for y ∈ E.
 (a) h is continuous.
 (b) If ‖y‖ > 1 + δ, then (1 + δ − ‖y‖)/δ < 0 and h(y) = 0. Thus h vanishes outside the compact set B_{1+δ}(0), so h ∈ C_c(E, ℝ).
 (c) h(y) ≥ 0 for all y, because min(1, max(0, ·)) ≥ 0.
 (d) If ‖y‖ ≤ 1, then (1 + δ − ‖y‖)/δ ≥ δ/δ = 1, so h(y) = 1 ≥ 1.
 (e) h ≤ 1_{B_{1+δ}(0)} pointwise. On B_{1+δ}(0), h ≤ 1 = 1_{B_{1+δ}(0)}. Off B_{1+δ}(0), h = 0 by (b).
 By (e), step 2 with s = 1 + δ, and integral_mono: ∫_P h dHⁿ = ∫ h dν ≤ ∫ 1_{B_{1+δ}(0)} dν = ω_n(1 + δ)ⁿ < b. With (c) and (d), h has all the properties required in (ii). ∎

The instance IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν from step 2 can be added as a local `have`, so no new named declaration is needed.
